title: Placement Training Test - Verbal Ability & Logical Reasoning - Day 14
description: A placement-style assessment focused on verbal ability, logical deduction, analytical reasoning, critical thinking, and professional communication.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The candidate gave a ___ explanation, covering every important point without unnecessary details.
If all successful applicants submitted their documents, and Ravi did not submit his documents, what can be concluded based only on these statements?
options: Ravi cannot be confirmed as a successful applicant.
Ravi did not attend the interview.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that is grammatically correct.
options: Each of the students have submitted their resume.
Each of the students has submitted their resume.
Each students has submitted their resume.
Each of the student have submitted their resume.

questions.question: Four people P, Q, R and S are standing in a line. P is to the left of Q. R is to the right of Q. S is to the left of P. Who is at the extreme left?
Statement: 'The company introduced flexible working hours, and employee satisfaction increased significantly.' Which conclusion is most reasonable?
options: Flexible working hours are the only reason for employee satisfaction.
Flexible working hours may have contributed to increased satisfaction.
Every employee prefers flexible working hours.
Employee satisfaction always increases when working hours change.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'substantiate'.
Five tasks A, B, C, D and E must be completed in order. A must occur before C. B must occur before D. E must be the last task. Which sequence is possible?
A statement says: 'Some developers are designers. All designers are creative.' Which conclusion definitely follows?
Which response is most appropriate when you disagree with a teammate's idea during a professional discussion?
options: I don't agree, so let's ignore it.
I see your point. However, could we also consider another approach?
Everyone knows my approach is better.

questions.question: A project team notices that a task repeatedly takes longer than estimated. What is the best analytical response?
options: Keep using the same estimate without investigation.
Blame the person performing the task.
Examine previous tasks, identify the cause of the delay, and improve future estimates.
Remove the task from the project.
